items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I also met my good friend and teacher, Theodore Carpenter... he had shown me some riffs back in Cincinnati.

ctx.x: In those days a musician got work by word of mouth. Someone would speak about him, praising the way he played, so that if a band leader heard about it, he would hire you. Orchestras were getting bigger, because when I started to play, there were no more than six or seven pieces, but later on, they got to be nine or ten. I remember once in Cincinnati that the Alex Jackson band was visiting the city from New York. He wanted a trumpet player, and he asked me come and see him at his hotel. I was working with Wes…

I went home after the week was over but I had lost my job at Western Union, and my father was not happy about me staying away longer than I was supposed to and had no job when I came back. A trumpet player named Theodore Carpenter had left a carnival and was now playing with Clarence Page and I met him. Carpenter had only one arm having lost his left one in an accident somewhere on a machine that had pulled his arm off up to the shoulder. But that was no handicap for him when it came to playing his horn. He could…

Carpenter was called "Wingy" by the musicians. Wings is slang for arms and there is not many instruments after a trumpet that a one-arm person can play. Because of the 3 valves, the trumpet can be held by the little finger and the thumb whereas a trumpet player with both hands can hold the trumpet with one hand and the other is free to manipulate the valves.
